I couldn't open the Runner's World or WIRED pages, so this comes mainly from SoundGuys' open-ear roundup. I haven't seen the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 or Bose Ultra Open reviews, so I can't rank them.

**Best picks for running**

| Pick | Price (per SoundGuys' Amazon listings) | Why it works for running |
|---|---|---|
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** (best budget) | $79.99 (list $99.99) | Adjustable ear hooks for a secure fit, IP55 rating, long battery life, 23 EQ presets. The touch controls are very sensitive. One owner got about 6 hours per charge, not the claimed 10. |
| **HUAWEI FreeClip 2** (clip-on) | $199.99 | Very light, IP57 rating, and either earbud fits either ear. SoundGuys specifically recommends it for runners. It's pricey, and sound quality depends on getting a good fit. |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** (best value) | $99 (list $149) | Strong bass for this category, IP54 rating, good controls and battery life. SoundGuys describes it as suited to athletes. |
| **Shokz OpenFit 2** (long runs) | $179.95 | Long battery life, and physical buttons that work with gloves. SoundGuys recommends it for endurance athletes. |
| **Sony LinkBuds Open** | $157.95 (list $229.99) | Long battery life and multipoint. It's less specifically aimed at runners. |
| **Apple AirPods 4** (iPhone users) | $138.86 | IP54 rating and a comfortable fit. It has no swappable tips, so the fit is one-size. Some owners found the sound too bright. |

**My take**
- **Best overall for most runners:** the Soundcore AeroFit 2. It's cheap, and the ear hooks and IP55 rating suit sweaty runs.
- **Best if you'll spend more:** the HUAWEI FreeClip 2 for light weight and sweat resistance, or the Shokz OpenFit 2 for marathon-length battery life.
- **Best on a budget with better bass:** the Nothing Ear (Open).

**Where to buy**
- Soundcore AeroFit 2: https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2. This is a third-party deals site. It claims code AFSC20 takes the price from $129.99 to $104 at Soundcore's store. That list price doesn't match the $79.99 Amazon price above, so compare both before buying.
- The SoundGuys roundup has retail links for the other picks: https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/

If you'd like bone-conduction models like the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, I can look for reviews of those next. I can also narrow this down by budget or phone type.
